title: Starter Snapshot: hero visuals, step-frames, and compact diagrams for onboarding landing
creator: Maya Hernandez
description: Goal: Produce a compact, modular visual system for the Quickstart landing that scales across hosted/dedicated/private product messaging. Deliverables: 1) Hero treatment (static + 3 responsive breakpoints + Lottie microinteraction variant), 2) Three compact step-frames (onboarding steps) designed to render cleanly as screenshots and inline docs diagrams, 3) A lightweight architecture diagram (hero-level) that explains 'Start -> Pin model -> Test -> Ship' flow without technical overload, 4) Export-ready screenshot pipeline (Figma export tokens, naming conventions, and device artboards), 5) High-contrast & RTL variants and guidance for a11y compliance. Success metrics: conversion uplift on Quickstart CTA in internal A/B, fewer support articles opened for first-run problems, and faster screenshot production for releases.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hero exported in PNG/SVG and Lottie; responsive snapshots for 320/768/1440 widths present.
2) Step-frames rendered as individual assets and a combined carousel; copy hooks and microcopy signed off by PM.
3) Architecture diagram simplified to 5 nodes or fewer, with an accessible text alternative description.
4) Figma file contains named export tokens and a short handoff doc.
5) All assets reviewed by Design Lead and PM, with implementation notes for engineering.
6) Screenshots validated on staging and smoke-tested against Console-2025.04 branch.
comments: 2025-02-11: Triage meeting with PM (Liam Chen) and Eng (Jon Ruiz). Decided focus on compact hero variants and single-line architecture diagram to reduce dev effort.
2025-02-18: Initial comps uploaded to Figma. Requested feedback from A11y and Marketing. Noted that motion will be optional for low-power devices.
2025-02-24: Design critique — adjusted color tokens to meet 4.5:1 contrast for body text; tightened step-frame copy to 6 words per step for screenshot clarity.
2025-03-01: Eng feasibility review (ENG-22011) — confirmed that Lottie microinteraction is acceptable; engineering asks for separate static fallback PNGs and a 2x density asset set.
2025-03-04: PM sign-off on hero copy; moving into final exports and preparing implementation notes for the Console-2025.04 rollout.
Reviewer notes: Marketing requests a variant that highlights 'Private deployment' benefits — added as a secondary hero state to the spec.
implementation_notes:
- Provide tokenized exports: hero_primary@1x, hero_primary@2x, hero_lottie.json, step_01@1x..step_03@2x.
- Include alt-text strings in the Figma handoff doc.
- Engineering should fetch assets from Drive path and reference naming convention in the PR.
- Motion: 6-8s subtle loop, with prefers-reduced-motion CSS fallback.
- For RTL: mirror layout and ensure iconography remains on consistent semantic side.
risks: Potential delays if engineering API surfaces change for feature flags that toggle hero variants; dependency on ENG-22011 for Lottie runtime. Also watch for content freeze windows for the upcoming release.
qa_checklist:
1) Visuals match Figma snapshots across 3 breakpoints.
2) Lottie falls back to PNG when motion disabled.
3) Alt text present in DOM and matches approved copy.
4) High-contrast and RTL variants reviewed by accessibility reviewer.
5) Screenshot pipeline verified: asset names and sizes correct in Drive.
notes_for_engineering:
- Coordinate with Eng on a feature-flag for hero variants (pm will open PM-3412).
- Provide a small CSS demo snippet and SVG fallbacks for older browsers.
- Ensure the Console-2025.04 branch includes a smoke test that loads the hero and verifies static fallback assets are served.
final_steps:
1) Export final assets and upload to Drive.
2) Attach implementation notes to PR and request review from Eng and Accessibility.
3) Notify Growth/Marketing for A/B scheduling.
4) Move ticket to In Review once PR is merged and artifacts are in Drive.
estimate_rationale: 5 points: 2 for initial exploration and comps, 2 for revisions and accessibility adjustments, 1 for final export and handoff.
